text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, a **~1,000 Wh** station gets you roughly 12-17 hours, and a **~2,000 Wh** station gets you a day or more. Whichever you pick, its inverter needs a surge rating of at least ~1,300 W and pure sine wave output.

## The three checks

1. **Surge watts (the one that most often fails).** The compressor spikes at startup. Sources put it at about 1,000-1,800 W for a standard fridge and up to ~2,400 W for large or older ones. If the station's surge rating is below that, it trips even with a full battery. ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/))
2. **Continuous watts.** A running fridge draws about 100-250 W, which almost any 1,000 W-class station covers. Add any other devices you'll run at the same time.
3. **Watt-hours.** The compressor cycles on only ~30-40% of the time, so a fridge averages far less than its running watts. Estimates range from about 41 W (an ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft model) to ~70 W (a more conservative example). That works out to roughly 1,000-1,400 Wh per day once you allow for inverter losses and headroom. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator))

## Rough sizing

| Capacity | Approx. fridge runtime | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| ~300 Wh | ~5 hours, and often fails the surge check | Not recommended for a fridge |
| ~1,000 Wh | ~12-17 hours | Short outages |
| ~2,000 Wh | ~33 hours | A full day or more |
| 3,000+ Wh | 2+ days | Multi-day outages, or a fridge plus other loads |

Runtimes come from [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) (35% duty cycle, 85% inverter efficiency) and [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator).

## Options that fit

- **Bluetti AC200L** (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W, 3,600 W surge, LiFePO4, expandable to 8 kWh): listed at $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. [Buy here](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l). That page is an affiliate listing, and its code was tested on 2026-10-21, so confirm at checkout.
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak, pure sine wave): listed at $699.99 after coupon. [See it at Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator).
- **Bluetti AC180** (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak), a budget pick for shorter outages: recently seen at $399-699. [Details from BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage). I didn't get a direct purchase link for it.

## Tips

- To find your fridge's real average, check its EnergyGuide label: kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760 = average watts. A plug-in energy meter is even better. Large side-by-sides with ice makers can average about double the ENERGY STAR figure.
- Keep the door shut during the outage, since that cuts compressor run time.
- If you also want a freezer, a CPAP, or lights, add their watts and Wh and size up. Expandable units like the AC200L let you add capacity later.
